prompt: Build the little bookkeeper a debugger uses to tell you which breakpoints were actually hit. Complete BreakpointHitReporter, then run the tests.
explanation: One TreeMap from line number to hit count is the whole state: TreeMap iterates in ascending key order, so neverHit and report come out sorted without any extra sorting step. The invariant that makes the class behave is that a key exists only for a registered breakpoint -- that is why execute checks containsKey before incrementing, and why a line with no breakpoint silently does nothing. addBreakpoint must guard with containsKey too, otherwise re-registering an existing breakpoint would overwrite its count with 0.
hints: A single Map<Integer, Integer> from line number to hit count holds everything; use TreeMap so the keys come back in ascending order.
addBreakpoint should only put a 0 when the key is absent -- otherwise re-registering wipes out the count.
Build report with a StringBuilder, appending "\n" before every row except the first so there is no trailing newline.
